summary.headline: Ahluwalia Contracts Q2 FY27 turnover rose 30% QoQ to ₹1,463.67 cr, but PAT margin of 3.78% and EBITDA margin of 7.58% remain well below last year's levels.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 turnover recovered sharply to ₹1,463.67 cr (up 30% QoQ, up 24% YoY) as delayed large North India projects ramped up after a weak Q1. EBITDA margin improved to 7.58% from 4.29% in Q1 but was down from 10.92% in Q2 FY26, and PAT fell 29% YoY to ₹55.86 cr. Management guided Q3 turnover down about 10% QoQ to roughly ₹1,300 cr because of NCR construction bans, with margins held near Q2 levels and an 8.5-9% margin target for FY28. Order book stood at ₹19,627.92 cr, but order inflow for FY27 to date was only ₹558.07 cr against a ~₹4,000 cr full-year guidance.

segments.name: NCR / North India
segments.commentary: About ₹520-525 cr of Q2 revenue came from NCR versus roughly ₹350 cr in Q1 (approximate, per management). Around half the order book is in NCR.

segments.name: Geographic order book mix
segments.commentary: Mumbai about 24%, East about 15% (Assam significant), Bangalore order book about ₹2,000 cr; company present in 19 states.

segments.name: CSMT (Mumbai railway)
segments.commentary: Billing ramping: about ₹80 cr billed in last month; management guides ~₹150 cr billing in Q3 and ~₹200 cr in Q4. Actual work done runs ~₹100-110 cr per month, with billing lagging due to railway processes.

segments.name: Central Vista (Delhi)
segments.commentary: Turnover ₹43 cr in October, expected ~₹60 cr in November and ₹60-70 cr in December; ~₹150 cr expected in Q3, ₹200 cr+ in Q4. FY27 guidance ~₹700 cr and FY28 ~₹1,000 cr unchanged.

segments.name: Gurugram Max hospital project
segments.commentary: Exempt from NCR ban; about ₹50 cr expected in Q3.

segments.name: Investment property (Kota commercial mart)
segments.commentary: Carrying value about ₹84 cr; rental income about ₹1.8 cr in Q2 per management, with some revenue expected in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 turnover expected around ₹1,300 cr, a roughly 10% QoQ dip, due to NCR construction ban (blanket ban in NCR until 20 Nov 2026; 1-1.5 months impact expected).
Q4 FY27 expected to be stronger than Q3; margins for H2 FY27 guided near Q2's 7.6% (conservative guidance).
FY27 revenue growth guidance of about 15% (management said 15%+), with FY28 revenue growth of 15-20%.
FY28 EBITDA margin improvement of at least one percentage point; management said 8.5-9% is doable, double digit not assured.
FY27 order inflow guidance of about ₹4,000 cr reiterated; about ₹1,000 cr won to date including post-September order of ~₹350 cr (Bennett University).
FY27 capex about ₹225 cr (₹142 cr in H1, ₹66 cr in Q2 per management), down from earlier guidance of over ₹300 cr and ~₹220 cr revised earlier.
Depreciation expected around ₹35 cr per quarter average in FY27 and ₹37-38 cr in FY28 (quarterly).
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at about ₹225 cr: ₹142 cr spent in H1 and ₹66 cr in Q2 (per management); capex focused on equipment such as cranes, batching plants, loaders, and specialised shuttering for high-rise and commercial buildings.
Management said it has reduced capex plans and will wait and watch given cyclicality of business, though order book is at an all-time high and existing equipment is considered sufficient.
Company said it is building up capacity to reach about ₹5,500 cr of annual revenue by end of this year (per management response on scale).
Gurugram/Delhi NCR projects halted by construction ban; Varanasi project (UP) deadline 27 June, may be completed earlier for inauguration ahead of UP elections.
demand_pricing: Net order book ₹19,627.92 cr as of 30 Sep 2026, to be executed over 3 to 3.5 years; earliest-completion example: Central Vista ~2 years with ~6 months elapsed.
FY27 order inflow to 30 Sep 2026 was ₹558.07 cr; company is currently L1 in one project worth ₹379 cr; ₹1,500 cr of bids submitted in private and public sector with ~₹5,000 cr total bid pipeline.
Contract mix: fixed-price about 9.19% of order book per management; EPC about 46% (management statement, unclear basis).

Labour escalation: minimum wage exemption threshold raised from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per month; about 85% of labour and staff now covered by EPF; about 50% of clients without labour escalation clause have agreed to minimum-wage-linked escalation.
Government contracts escalate on WPI; private contracts reference basic rates of volatile materials such as bitumen, RMC and steel. New bids include escalation clauses.
Material costs up about 4-5 percentage points of revenue due to project mix (EPC contracts such as Central Vista and CSMT where materials are billed as they arrive).

qa_highlights.question: Why did H1 margins fall, and what is the outlook for FY27 and FY28 revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was hit by slow start on large North India (MCR) projects and labour cost revisions; Q2 recovered. Management expects FY27 margins similar to Q2, FY27 revenue growth of 15%, and FY28 growth of 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 be weaker than Q4 going forward given the seasonal NCR pollution curbs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: Q3 has been hit by a 10% dip in past year and is expected to dip again to about ₹1,300 cr; Q4 expected to be strongest, with Q2 and Q4 seen as best quarters of the calendar year if pollution persists.

qa_highlights.question: Why margin guidance of 8.5-9% rather than double digits, and does a share buyback make sense given ~₹1,000 cr treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 8.5-9% doable for FY28 and said double digit is difficult to predict; it cited headwinds and conservative guidance. On buyback, management said it would consider the suggestion but prioritises supply-chain control and efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Why are peer BLK-type margins converging with the company's margins and what explains the cost gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher staff costs (~₹12.5 cr QoQ increase), minimum wage and EPF changes, and higher scale-related overheads; management compared with L&T (5.5% vs its 7.5%) to argue cost structure is not inefficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Can price escalation help margins sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Government contracts escalate on WPI with a lag; private contracts escalate on material/labour indices. About half of clients without labour clauses have agreed to minimum-wage escalation; new bids include escalation clauses.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of NCR vs non-NCR revenue and Q3 key projects?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹520-525 cr of Q2 revenue from NCR versus about ₹350 cr in Q1 (approximate). Q3 relies on Central Vista (~₹150 cr) and Max Gurugram hospital (~₹50 cr), both exempt from the ban.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Mumbai CSMT and Gurugram/Jharkhand-type projects and CSMT revenue expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: CSMT billing ~₹80 cr last month, targeting ~₹150 cr in Q3 and ~₹200 cr in Q4; Mumbai Govandi/Gubi project has not received notice to proceed so no Q3 revenue expected.

qa_highlights.question: Will the DLF downtown project's ₹200 cr order increase be commodity inflation or scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Management indicated the ₹200 cr increase reflects a scope increase rather than just commodity price inflation.

risks_watch: Q3 FY27 turnover guided at about ₹1,300 cr (~10% QoQ dip) with NCR blanket construction ban in place until 20 Nov 2026; management also expects the ban may be extended depending on AQI.
FY27 order inflow of ~₹558 cr to 30 Sep 2026 against ~₹4,000 cr full-year guidance; ~₹1,000 cr won to date per management, so a large back-end order flow is needed.

Margin pressure from EPF change (~0.5 ppt impact), electromechanical price increases not yet fully covered by escalation clauses, and uncertain Middle East supply chain; H2 margins guided near Q2's 7.6%.

Billing lag on CSMT railway project and Mumbai Govandi/Gubi project with no notice to proceed yet, so no Q3 revenue expected from it; Central Vista and Max Gurugram hospital are the main exempt-project Q3 revenue sources.
Capex cut to about ₹225 cr for FY27 from over ₹300 cr; management cited cyclicality, which raises questions on long-term capacity for the stated ~₹5,500 cr revenue scale.
Interest-bearing mobilisation advance (~32% of ₹939 cr) and unbilled revenue of ₹925 cr could weigh on working capital and cash conversion.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the Q2 recovery and on order book execution, but cautious on margins, guiding H2 FY27 only to Q2 levels and declining to commit to double-digit margins, citing headwinds and conservative guidance. It was evasive on the buyback suggestion, on the investment property monetisation, and on the exact NCR revenue split, offering only approximate figures.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15%+ backed by a ₹19,628 cr order book (3-3.5 yr execution) and named projects (Central Vista ~₹700 cr, CSMT ₹150 cr Q3/₹200 cr Q4), but Q3 turnover guided down ~10% QoQ on NCR construction ban and FY27 order inflow is only ₹558 cr against a ₹4,000 cr target, so the 4-quarter outlook is flat.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 7.58% vs 4.29% in Q1 and 10.92% in Q2 FY26; H2 FY27 guided near 7.6% and FY28 8.5-9% called doable, but double digit not assured and material costs up 4-5 ppt of revenue on mix.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FY27 capex cut to about ₹220-225 cr from over ₹300 cr, management says existing equipment is sufficient and it will wait and watch given cyclicality.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15%+ and FY28 at 15-20% on a ₹19,628 cr order book executed over 3-3.5 years, though Q3 turnover is guided down ~10% QoQ to ~₹1,300 cr on NCR ban.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was pruned to about ₹220-225 cr and management said it will wait and watch, so no fresh capex announcement is signalled despite an all-time-high order book.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 order inflow is only ₹558 cr to 30 Sep against ₹4,000 cr guidance and H2 margins guided only to Q2 levels, so upside to guidance is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 turnover guided ~10% lower to ~₹1,300 cr with NCR ban possibly extended per AQI, and FY27 order inflow needs ~₹3,400 cr more in H2 to hit ₹4,000 cr.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed on the call.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow reaching ₹4,000 cr
rows.why: Only ₹558 cr booked to 30 Sep against ₹4,000 cr target, though ~₹1,000 cr won to date per management and ₹1,500 cr bids submitted with ₹5,000 cr pipeline.

rows.label: Mobilisation advance and unbilled revenue unwind
rows.why: Mobilisation advance ₹939 cr (about 32% interest-bearing) and unbilled revenue ₹925 cr, with CSMT billing lagging actual work of ₹100-110 cr per month against ₹80 cr billed last month.

rows.label: Escalation clauses recovering cost inflation
rows.why: About 50% of clients without labour clauses agreed to minimum-wage escalation and new bids carry escalation, but EPF change costs ~0.5 ppt and electromechanical costs are not yet fully covered.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q2 recovery, order book execution and Central Vista/CSMT billing, but cautious on margins, guiding H2 to Q2 levels and declining to commit to double-digit margins; analysts pushed on margin gap, buyback, and the thin FY27 order inflow.
